paragraphs: Dip Mafia (formerly HODL-bot) is an automated algo-trading signal system that identifies deeply undervalued stocks during market crashes using 200-period Bollinger Bands and dual MACD crossovers, then delivers actionable buy signals with market sentiment to Telegram and Discord, fully automated via GitHub Actions.

Philosophy: Buy the crash, hold forever. This bot watches 150+ NSE stocks (the six7 watchlist ∪ your real holdings) and alerts when they hit statistically extreme lows with confirmed momentum reversal. No day-trading, no exits, just long entries at high-conviction dips. We never sell. Sell / red signals are indications only: they flag technical weakness for awareness; Dip Mafia does not execute exits. The strategy is buy dips and HODL. The watchlist is the union of two lists: six7.txt (the six7 watchlist — the Top N by Fundamental Score, curated by a separate fundamental scorer) and…

paragraphs: The ADK-Powered Travel Planner is a multi-agent travel-planning application. A host service coordinates specialist services for flights, stays, and activities, while a Streamlit UI provides the user-facing workflow.
Generated flights, stays, and activities are illustrative suggestions only; they are not live availability, live prices, or bookable offers.

Documentation: the full docs are a Mintlify site in docs/, organized as tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation. New here? Start with the tutorial, docs/tutorials/first-trip-plan.mdx. To browse the site locally, install the CLI (npm i -g mint), then run mint dev in docs/ and open
features: Multi-Agent Architecture: Orchestrates specialized agents for different travel aspects.
Pluggable LLM Provider: Ollama (Meta Llama, self-hosted) or OpenAI gpt-4o-mini (cloud), selected by LLMPROVIDER.
Structured Responses: Requests JSON-schema-constrained output from either provider and validates it against shared Pydantic contracts.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Flight, Stay, and Activities add relevant Wikivoyage passages to their prompts, retrieved with LlamaIndex (from Chroma when self-hosted, or a committed file index on Vercel), and trip…
Containerized Runtime: One Dockerfile with separate API and UI images, so each installs only the dependencies it needs.

whatItDoes.text: The ADK-Powered Travel Planner is a multi-agent travel-planning application. A host service coordinates specialist services for flights, stays, and activities, while a Streamlit UI provides the user-facing workflow.

requirements.text: Project status: the self-hosted setup is the supported way to run the project.
npm i -g vercel, vercel login, then vercel link --yes --project travel-planner from the repository root.
The Host API key is what clients must send as X-API-Key; generate a long random value.
Any other client must send the key too, for example curl -H "X-API-Key: " -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @trip.json /run.
If your AWS CLI signs in with aws login, run eval "$(aws configure export-credentials --format env)" in the same shell before each Terraform command; Terraform can't read those credentials directly.

repositories.name: Scrip
repositories.description: Weft - one token woven from real stocks: a corporate-actions indexer and the onchain weave that mints it.

paragraphs: One token, woven from real stocks. Weft is an onchain index fund built from Coinbase Tokenized Stocks on Base: weave USDC in, receive a self-custodial basket token holding Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Tesla, unwind back to USDC anytime. Dividends handled. Every step provable.

The sponsor's own request-for-builders names it: composable single-name stocks with deep underlying liquidity, turned into personal portfolios. The liquidity is real and measured: AAPLc/USDC holds $1.36M on Aerodrome Slipstream ($1.6M daily volume), NVDAc/USDC $2.6M.

And the part a generic basket gets wrong: tokenized stock dividends are not paid in cash. The issuer raises an onchain multiplier (UIMultiplierUpdated) and one B20 token quietly becomes more than one share. Their docs warn: "One B20 token does not permanently equal one share." A basket that reads raw balances breaks silently on the first corporate action. Weft prices its inventory through scaledBalanceOf and values it with the Coinbase total-return Chainlink feeds, so dividends accrue to holders and weights stay true. No dividend has executed yet (every registry multiplier reads 1.0 today);…

whatItDoes.text: One token, woven from real stocks. Weft is an onchain index fund built from Coinbase Tokenized Stocks on Base: weave USDC in, receive a self-custodial basket token holding Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Tesla, unwind back to USDC anytime. Dividends handled. Every step provable.

repositories.name: demo-spa-source-code
repositories.description: A React tutorial project based on the "React - Путь Самурая" course from IT-Incubator

paragraphs: This is a learning project created to master React and related technologies. The project is based on the "React - Путь Самурая" course from IT-Incubator. It is a simplified version of a social network, built as a Single Page Application (SPA), where I implemented core features like user authentication, profile management, and post creation. Additionally, I developed a real-time chat feature using WebSocket. I also implemented a paginated user search, allowing users to browse through profiles efficiently.

At its core, the project leverages React and TypeScript, providing a strong foundation for building scalable and type-safe components. To handle routing, I used React Router DOM. For state management, I integrated Redux alongside React Redux, utilizing Redux Thunk for handling asynchronous actions and Reselect for efficient state selection. For forms implementation, I used both Redux Form and Formik, ensuring solid validation and user-friendly interactions. To handle HTTP requests, I relied on Axios, which allowed me to interact with APIs smoothly, and querystring for encoding URL parameters.…

Throughout the codebase, I have included extensive comments to explain the logic, structure, and purpose of each component, function, and module. These comments are designed to make the code more accessible to other developers, as well as to serve as a learning resource for myself when revisiting the project in the future.

repositories.name: fraud-detection-engine
repositories.description: Real-time fraud decisioning engine with anomaly scoring, explainable policy rules, alert triage, and a live operations console. Synthetic demo data.

paragraphs: Real-time transaction risk decisioning, alert triage, and model observability as a single deployable application.
Live demo: sentinel-fraud-ops.onrender.com (Render, Singapore; synthetic data)

Sentinel is the fraud decision layer for a fictional payments company, Meridian Pay. It ingests card-authorisation events, computes a behavioural anomaly score and an explainable policy score in the request path, returns allow / review / block, and persists the complete evidence behind every decision. The React console is an operations surface, not a dashboard bolted onto a notebook: alerts can be assigned and resolved, thresholds can be changed at runtime, historical data can be replayed, and the live feed is pushed over Server-Sent Events.

repositories.name: reconocimiento-digitos-manuscritos
repositories.description: De plantillas con SSIM a una CNN en PyTorch: 7 métodos comparados en MNIST (99,4 %), demo con webcam y web en Streamlit con ONNX.

paragraphs: Comparativa de siete métodos para reconocer dígitos escritos a mano (MNIST), desde la comparación con plantillas mediante SSIM hasta una red convolucional en PyTorch, todos evaluados con la misma partición y sin fuga de datos. La mejor red se exporta a ONNX y reconoce dígitos en tiempo real con la webcam y en una web hecha con Streamlit.
La web con una foto simulada de un 4 escrito con bolígrafo (un dígito del test de MNIST pasado a papel, con sombra y ruido).

English summary. Seven handwritten-digit classifiers on MNIST (SSIM template matching and nearest neighbour, HOG + linear SVM, an MLP, LeNet and LeNet with data augmentation in PyTorch) compared on the same split with a held-out test set. The augmented CNN reaches 99.4 % test accuracy and keeps 98.9 % on rotated, shifted and rescaled digits, while the plain LeNet trained without augmentation drops to 82.5 %. Includes a real-time webcam demo (OpenCV) with an MNIST-style preprocessing pipeline and a Streamlit app that runs the model with ONNX Runtime.
features: 99,4 % de exactitud en las 10.000 imágenes de test con una CNN entrenada con aumento de datos.
98,9 % con dígitos girados, desplazados y reescalados, frente al 82,5 % de la LeNet entrenada sin aumento.
94,6 % entrenando con solo 100 imágenes, y menos de 1 ms por imagen en CPU.

repositories.description: SmartGrid AI: calibrated early-warning for power-transformer failures — GRU + temporal attention, leakage-safe evaluation, ONNX streaming engine, FastAPI + React. Live demo.

paragraphs: Real-time predictive-maintenance and early-warning platform for power-transformer sensor streams.

A GRU + temporal-attention model reads a 12-hour window of causal features and estimates the risk of a failure within the next 2 hours. Its score is calibrated, given a model-confidence estimate, explained, and turned into alerts by a streaming engine. The engine is served through FastAPI and a React/TypeScript operations center with Incident Replay and a guided Demo Mode that run the real engine on held-out data.
Live website: . The real engine runs as a serverless function on Vercel's free tier, and visitors drive it:
features: Scenario Lab: inject a fault (type, severity, precursor length) into a synthetic transformer stream and watch
Upload & Score: run your own CSV of readings through the engine.
Results pages: Failure Intelligence, Model Lab and Methodology.

LCRL automatically shapes a synchronous reward function on-the-fly. This enables any off-the-shelf RL algorithm to synthesise policies that yield traces which probabilistically satisfy the LTL property. LCRL produces policies that are certified to satisfy the given LTL property with maximum probability.

repositories.name: tracelint
repositories.description: A deterministic linter for agent runs — reads the execution trace and flags structural bugs (ignored errors, schema violations, loops) with evidence. No LLM judge.

paragraphs: tracelint checks an agent's execution trace for structural defects, locally or in CI. It can read trace files directly or import traces from your existing observability platform.

It reads what a tool-calling agent actually did — the execution trace — and flags structural bugs deterministically, with the exact evidence and a CI exit code. It runs after the run, on the trace, not on your code, and no second model ever judges it. Model-as-judge detection of these defects is unreliable (published trace-error benchmarks show low localization accuracy); many of them are structurally decidable and need no judge — that is the entire premise of the tool.

Website: tracelint.com — what it catches, how it works, and how to wire it into CI. See a live demo report — the constructed validation suite (one planted instance of every defect, clean controls, and legitimate-but-suspicious cases) plus the robust-vs-buggy recovery scorecard, generated by tracelint demo.

whatItDoes.text: tracelint checks an agent's execution trace for structural defects, locally or in CI. It can read trace files directly or import traces from your existing observability platform.

repositories.name: Mini-LLM
repositories.description: A ground-up LLM engineering project: tokenizer → architecture → training → scaling laws → inference. Starts at 80M, engineered to scale into 1B+ models with minimal changes. Clean, research-ready code for anyone serious about understanding and building LLMs from first principles.

paragraphs: A production-grade implementation of a decoder-only transformer language model, built from scratch with modern best practices. This project demonstrates the complete pipeline from raw text to a functioning LLM capable of text generation.
There are many "build your own GPT" tutorials out there. So why Mini-LLM?
features: RoPE (Rotary Position Embeddings): Better extrapolation to longer sequences than learned positions
RMSNorm: Faster and simpler than LayerNorm, used in LLaMA
SwiGLU: Gated activation function, empirically better than GELU/ReLU
Grouped Query Attention: Reduces KV cache size for faster inference
Memory-Mapped Data Loading: Train on TB-scale datasets with minimal RAM

repositories.name: clear-hash
repositories.description: A digital tamper-proof seal for software that verifies downloaded apps match their exact original source code.

paragraphs: A digital tamper-proof seal for software. ClearHash verifies that downloaded packages match their exact original source code byte-for-byte.

Think of ClearHash like a verified safety seal on food packaging. When developers publish software, bad actors can secretly alter the final download. ClearHash independently rebuilds the software from scratch and checks every byte to prove nobody modified the program between the original source code and your computer.

ClearHash acts as a pre-install gatekeeper. It fetches a package, verifies its SLSA attestation through Sigstore and Rekor, rebuilds it from the attested source commit in an isolated Docker container, and compares the rebuilt file tree against the registry artifact. If anything differs, the install is blocked.

whatItDoes.text: A digital tamper-proof seal for software. ClearHash verifies that downloaded packages match their exact original source code byte-for-byte.

paragraphs: We introduce DreamLite, a compact and unified on-device diffusion model (0.39B) that seamlessly supports both text-to-image generation and text-guided image editing within a single network architecture.

Built upon a pruned mobile U-Net backbone, DreamLite unifies multimodal conditioning through In-Context Spatial Concatenation directly in the latent space. repositories.name: DISHA-platform
repositories.description: Consolidates India's scattered disaster alerts and news into one verified, map-based feed, letting citizens report incidents and locate nearby emergency services.

paragraphs: Disaster Intelligence and Situational Hazard Awareness Platform — a full-stack web application that aggregates, verifies, and visualizes real-time disaster and emergency data for India, combining government data feeds, AI-assisted news verification, and citizen incident reporting on an interactive map.
Live deployment: disha-platform.vercel.app (frontend) · API on Render (backend)

DISHA ingests disaster-related information from multiple official and open sources — India's National Center for Seismology (earthquakes), NDMA's SACHET alert system (government warnings), and news feeds cross-checked by Google's Gemini model — and unifies them into a single, filterable event feed. It also lets signed-in citizens submit their own incident reports with location and photo evidence, and surfaces nearby emergency services (hospitals, police, fire stations) for a given location.
features: BACKEND/ — a Python FastAPI service that runs the data-ingestion pipelines, exposes a REST API, and talks to MongoDB.
FRONTEND/ — a React + Vite single-page application that consumes the API and renders the map, dashboards, and forms.
Unified disaster event feed (/api/events) merging earthquakes, NDMA SACHET alerts, and AI-verified news into one normalized dataset.
Live interactive map on the landing page (LiveDisasterMap.jsx) built directly on the core Leaflet library, with severity/category styling, time-range filtering, and an emergency-services overlay.
Earthquake ingestion from the official NCS RISEQ portal (app/sources/riseq.py), with UTC normalization and India-relevance filtering.

repositories.name: verification-is-identification
repositories.description: A research framework for finding what you can know and do without knowing the whole system

paragraphs: Different visible spectra can produce the same colour reading for a specified observer under fixed conditions. This is metamerism. That reading alone does not identify the spectrum. Some questions about the source can still be answered exactly, and some operations on it can still be chosen with grounds.

This repository studies that situation in general: what a partial view of an unknown source determines, which actions it supports before the source is identified, and what the result must keep for whoever continues the work. The arguments are in 35 papers. The part written as Swift types is checked by the compiler, and a second reader checks a fragment of it separately.
Start with Verification Is Identification for the criterion, the constructions and their connection to the source being studied.
features: The action law above, with what a continuation must keep after the source, the access or the participant changes.
A typed record of the research: 199 protocols, one per claim, with constructions the compiler checks and expected refusals that must keep failing.
A second reader that names what it refuses, and a finite contract against which another implementation of that reader is checked.
Worked models, among them the three sources above and the company of the showcase package.

whatItDoes.text: Different visible spectra can produce the same colour reading for a specified observer under fixed conditions. This is metamerism. That reading alone does not identify the spectrum. Some questions about the source can still be answered exactly, and some operations on it can still be chosen with grounds.

Full training loop: data loading, Adam + cosine annealing + AMP mixed precision + optional VGG perceptual loss, PSNR/SSIM evaluation, TorchScript export.

Three shipped weights: SR ×4 (PSNR 27.47), SR ×2 (PSNR 32.35) and low-light (PSNR 18.32) — each beats its classical baseline; classical methods remain as automatic fallback if a weight is ever missing.
Quantitative comparison: classical baselines vs. self-trained models on the same validation set; scripts and per-epoch logs are committed and recomputable.

Engineering: CI runs the tests behind a coverage gate, audits dependencies, and builds the frontend; the Docker image runs as a non-root user; the API enforces per-IP rate limiting and ships documentation.

whatItDoes.text: PixelForge: an end-to-end image restoration pipeline

requirements.text: Self-host the FastAPI backend + Next.js frontend

The FastAPI backend (serve/app.py) and the Next.js frontend (web/) are part of the same codebase and can be self-hosted; web/ posts to serve/app.py, which picks the ML engine for a task/scale when a weight is loaded, otherwise a classical baseline.

repositories.description: Rescue whole websites from the Wayback Machine.

paragraphs: Rescue whole websites from the Wayback Machine.

Wayback-Archive is a command-line tool that downloads an archived website from the Wayback Machine and rebuilds it as a folder you can open offline. It fetches every page and asset it can find in the snapshot, rewrites the links to local paths and removes the Wayback Machine's own toolbar, scripts and URL prefixes, so the copy looks like the site did on that day. wget --mirror and httrack do not understand Wayback Machine URLs; this does.
features: Saves HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and fonts, following links in HTML, CSS and JavaScript until nothing is left to fetch.
Every link in the copy points at the local file, so pages open and lead to each other without the Wayback toolbar or its URL prefixes.
A page or file missing from the snapshot is looked up at up to three other Wayback timestamps (a day either side and a week earlier) before it is given up on.
A capture that is an archived error or a Cloudflare challenge page is replaced with the nearest good capture.
Google Fonts are saved locally, and a font the archive returns as an HTML error page is dropped instead of breaking the page.

whatItDoes.text: Rescue whole websites from the Wayback Machine.

paragraphs: The open-source AI assistant that carries your family's mental load.

Italian families juggle an absurd amount of recurring bureaucracy: bollo auto, revisione, RCA, TARI, PagoPA notices, ID card renewals, utility bills, pediatrician appointments, antibiotic schedules. FamilySherpa makes tracking all of it passive: you forward a voice note, a photo, or a PDF to a Telegram bot (or upload it in the app), and the AI extracts what it is, when it's due, how much it costs, and which family asset it belongs to. You tap Conferma and forget about it — the app remembers for you.

The core loop works end to end: send the bot a voice note, a photo, a PDF or a text message, and it comes back with what it understood plus one-tap confirm/cancel buttons; confirming writes real deadlines, expenses, therapies and medicines, which you can review and correct from the in-app Inbox, or manage by hand from the Asset, Scadenze and Armadietto screens (create/edit/archive assets, add deadlines with Italian smart defaults, mark them paid with automatic recurrence roll-over, photograph a medicine box or log a therapy and tick off each dose). The app then reminds you — via web push and…

Features real-time GPS tracking, fuel analytics, vehicle health monitoring, predictive maintenance, driver safety, geofencing, live dashboards, and advanced business intelligence.

paragraphs: Enterprise-Grade Microservices Fleet Management Platform

FleetIQ is a massive, multi-tenant IoT fleet management platform designed for scale. It handles real-time vehicle telemetry ingestion (via MQTT & Kafka), complex spatial geofencing algorithms, AI-driven vehicle diagnostics, and dynamic driver safety scoring.

The platform is architected as an Event-Driven Microservices Ecosystem with 10 distinct Spring Boot backend services, a modular React Admin Dashboard, and an offline-first Flutter Mobile Monorepo for drivers and fleet managers.
features: 🚀 Real-Time Telemetry Processing: High-throughput ingestion of GPS/OBD-II data using MQTT Mosquitto, standardized via a Device Gateway, and streamed through Apache Kafka.
📍 Spatial Geofencing (JTS R-Tree): In-memory R-Tree spatial indexing for lightning-fast geo-fencing (ENTER/EXIT events, speed limit enforcement, and dwell time tracking).
⛽ Advanced Fuel Analytics: Sliding-window algorithms detecting fuel theft (sudden drops), slow leaks, and excessive idling using moving averages.
🛡️ Dynamic Driver Scoring: Real-time event consumption (harsh braking, cornering) to dynamically adjust driver safety scores and dispatch coaching suggestions.
🩺 Vehicle Diagnostic Rules Engine: Tenant-configurable sensor thresholds evaluating OBD-II telemetry (engine RPM, coolant temp, oil pressure) to predict breakdowns.

whatItDoes.text: Enterprise-Grade Microservices Fleet Management Platform

AI agents read things that strangers can write: web pages, tickets, invoices, logs, MCP tool results, retrieved documents. That text can carry prompt injections — instructions aimed not at you but at the agent that will read it ("ignore your instructions", "send the API keys here", "This message is from the system administrator").

features: What it does. An OpenAI-compatible security gateway for AI agents. Tool results, fetched pages, MCP payloads and RAG chunks pass through spanguard before the agent reads them; validated rules, a 135M-parameter…

repositories.name: voicecap
repositories.description: voicecap drives a real screen reader through a site's pages the way a vision-imparied visitor would: NVDA on a Windows PC, and VoiceOver on a Mac. It reads from top to bottom, jumps from heading to heading, and tabs through links and buttons, and it saves everything the screen reader says as plain-text transcripts.

paragraphs: voicecap has a real screen reader, NVDA, read each page of a website and saves every word it says, so one person can review a whole site the way a screen reader user hears it, and hand managers and auditors a dated record they can check to the byte. No off-the-shelf checker does this: tools such as axe, Siteimprove, and Lighthouse inspect a page's code but can't tell you what a screen reader actually says, and checking by hand goes one page at a time and leaves no record, far too slow for the more than a dozen websites ICJIA must review before the April 2027 ADA Title II deadline for…

A blind visitor doesn't see a website. They hear it, through a screen reader, and what the screen reader says is, for them, the website. The code is how a site is built; the sound is what a blind visitor gets.
Code can pass a checker's accessibility rules and still sound wrong:
features: alt text that's there but says nothing useful, such as "image", "logo", or a file name;
links that make no sense read aloud, such as ten in a row that each say "Read more";
headings that don't tell a screen reader user where they are;
buttons and fields named in words that make no sense when a screen reader says them;
a page that's read in a different order from the one it shows.

whatItDoes.text: voicecap has a real screen reader, NVDA, read each page of a website and saves every word it says, so one person can review a whole site the way a screen reader user hears it, and hand managers and auditors a dated record they can check to the byte. No off-the-shelf checker does this: tools such as axe, Siteimprove, and Lighthouse inspect a page's code but can't tell you what a screen reader actually says, and checking by hand goes one page at a time and leaves no record, far too slow for the more than a dozen websites ICJIA must review before the April 2027 ADA Title II deadline for…

requirements.text: There's no server, no account, and no outside service: what NVDA says is saved on that PC, and goes only where the person running voicecap sends it.

Then comes the record of it, word for word, with the home folder replaced by %USERPROFILE% (or ), the event log's lines from that attempt, and, from 0.17.0, NVDA's own warnings and errors from the same time (nvda-log in the table's "From" column), each after its level, as in "ERROR: Error accepting connection", so a warning is told from an error.

repositories.name: ironclaw
repositories.description: Security-first, self-hosted AI agents - isolation you can prove, not just promise.

paragraphs: Self-hosted AI agents you do not have to trust.
Each one runs sealed in a sandbox that provably cannot phone home, read your host, or rewrite its own rules.

IronClaw runs autonomous AI agents on infrastructure you control, reached through the chat apps you already use. Each agent can read, write, schedule, and reply like any assistant, but it lives inside a sealed sandbox with network=none: it reaches the model only through a host proxy, and it cannot change its own configuration. repositories.name: ai-ops-assistant
repositories.description: A constrained, auditable AI operations agent that earns permission before acting. Most AI agents freestyle with full tool access. Warrant does the opposite: every tool is gated by permission tiers (auto / log-and-run / needs-approval), every action is fully traced, and high-impact actions (like sending emails) require human approval.

paragraphs: An AI operations assistant that doesn't act without earning the right to.

Most "AI agent" demos let the model freestyle — call any tool, chain any action, and execute without guardrails. Warrant is the opposite bet: a constrained, deterministic agent where every tool sits behind a permission tier, every decision leaves a trace, and anything that leaves the system (like sending an email to a real customer) waits for human approval — and that approval reports back honestly, not optimistically.

A warrant is permission that has to be earned before an action proceeds. That is exactly how Warrant behaves. The model never decides what it is allowed to do — it proposes, the permission layer decides, and the system reports back honestly about what actually happened.

repositories.name: Falcon
repositories.description: Falcon is a causal audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) model

paragraphs: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
Wendi Sang\, Kai Li\, Yifan Li, Jianqiang Huang, Xiaolin Hu \Equal contribution
arXiv paper · Project page · Live demo · Hugging Face Space · Falcon Studio
features: RealSSA is a realistic simulated-scene AVTSE benchmark with near-/far-field interfering speech in four scene types, plus a real-recorded evaluation split.
Falcon is a causal AVTSE framework. Its AudioBlock performs multi-scale time-frequency separation in a single encoder–decoder pass.
An encoder-space speaker contrastive loss suppresses near-field leakage at zero inference cost and transfers across backbones.

repositories.description: Open-source racing sim that runs in your browser: 500 Hz vehicle physics, thermal tyres, open-wheelers and a GT3, AI races, ghosts, P2P multiplayer and wheel force feedback.

paragraphs: ▶ Play in your browser · Features · Controls · Development · Credits

LibreCorsa is an open-source racing simulator that runs entirely in the browser. It has rigid-body vehicle dynamics at 500 Hz, a thermal tyre model, 2026-regulation open-wheelers and a GT3 car. There are four circuits, AI races, ghosts and replays, and peer-to-peer multiplayer. It works with a keyboard, gamepad, touch screen or a force-feedback wheel. Nothing to install, and no server: it ships as a static site.
LibreCorsa is an independent fan project. It is not affiliated with Formula 1, the FIA, any team or any circuit.
features: 500 Hz fixed-step integration (4 × 2 kHz sub-steps): a 3D rigid body with each wheel riding the real track surface.

Tyres: a Pacejka-style slip curve with combined slip, load sensitivity, carcass relaxation and a load-dependent rolling radius. A 9-node thermal model (inner/middle/outer × surface/bulk/carcass) sets the grip window,…

Chassis: double-wishbone kinematics with roll centres from the hardpoints, springs, dampers, bump stops, anti-roll bars and heave elements. There's a preload / power / coast limited-slip differential and thermal brakes…
Aero: ride-height-sensitive wings and floor, altitude-corrected air density, and dirty air behind other cars. 2026 active aero switches between Z-mode (cornering) and X-mode (straights).

Surfaces: one data table for road, kerb, sausage kerb, run-off, pit lane, grass and gravel, with dry and wet friction, rolling resistance, a bump ripple you feel through the wheel, vibration and whether it counts for…

repositories.name: Checkbox-Detection
repositories.description: Checkbox Detection Model for Scanned Documents

paragraphs: In this project, I provided 2 models (classification and detection models) trained on the existing YOLOv8 weights. They are uploaded in my Hugging Face Space of the project. If you feel the need to use or fine-tune the models in any parts of your work, please cite this repository. Thank you, and don't forget to give this repo a 🌟!

The biggest challenge when I approach this problem is the lack of public datasets that contain documents with checkbox annotations. There are only either images of checkboxes alone, or images of scanned documents. As a result, the solution comes down to generating a sufficiently large annotated dataset of document with checkboxes.

Although the idea of using the Copy-Paste technique in augmenting data is simple, how to make that augmented dataset works well with the existing YOLO architecture is the most difficult part, which takes a lot of trial and error. Throughout this process, I experimented with different ways to paste the checkboxes onto the documents, which include pasting boxes contiguously in horizontal and vertical directions, pasting distractors, adding "background" images, pasting while also avoiding text blocks (using the Document Layout Analysis model I created), etc. I ended with over 10,000 images for…

repositories.name: kubeintellect
repositories.description: An AI SRE for Kubernetes: connects to your cluster, investigates with real tools, explains the root cause in plain English, and executes the fix only after you approve it. Peer-reviewed — Journal of Grid Computing, 2026.

paragraphs: Human-governed AI SRE for Kubernetes — chat with your cluster in plain English.
Created & maintained by Mohsen Seyedkazemi Ardebili

Ask why a pod is broken → get the root cause. Ask it to change something → it stops and waits for you. A real session against a live cluster, recorded end to end — nothing is cut, only the waiting is compressed.
features: KubeIntellect is an open-source framework for conversational, natural-language Kubernetes operations — root-cause analysis, live diagnostics, and human-approved cluster actions.
It is for platform engineers, DevOps engineers, SREs, and Kubernetes operators who want to troubleshoot and manage clusters in plain English.
It helps you diagnose incidents faster by correlating kubectl state, Prometheus metrics, and Loki logs through a coordinator that delegates to pod, metrics, logs, and events subagents.
Use KubeIntellect when you want conversational operations with a hard safety gate on every destructive action.
It is different from read-only AI diagnostics tools because it can also act — scale, restart, delete — but only after explicit human approval, gated by RBAC (admin / operator / readonly).

whatItDoes.text: Human-governed AI SRE for Kubernetes — chat with your cluster in plain English.

requirements.text: It requires an OpenAI or Azure OpenAI API key and Python 3.12+.

repositories.name: picogame
repositories.description: A fast, retained-mode 2D game engine for MCUs

paragraphs: picogame is a small 2D game engine for the PicoPad - a pocket handheld (320×240 screen, D-pad + a few buttons, RP2040 with little RAM) running CircuitPython. The heavy lifting - sprites, tilemaps, a retained scene with automatic dirty-rectangle redraw, blit effects - is a native C module built into the firmware; on top of it sits a set of small Python helper libraries and a desktop simulator, so you write games in plain Python and run them on your PC before ever touching hardware.

This repository is the public collection: finished games, short demos, feature examples, step-by-step tutorials, the simulator, and the asset tools - everything you need to learn the engine and build for it. The engine itself and the helper library live in their own repos (see The wider picogame project below).

repositories.name: FixMySlop
repositories.description: The slop linter for the AI-agent era: catch AI slop in UI and code in milliseconds, then let your agent fix it.

paragraphs: The slop linter for the AI-agent era. FixMySlop catches the things AI coding agents get wrong — the purple-gradient landing page, the // ... existing code ... that silently deleted half a file, the npm package that doesn't exist, the OpenAI key in NEXTPUBLIC — in milliseconds, without an LLM. Then it hands a precise fix list to the agent you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini) and re-scans to prove it's fixed.
Try it without installing: paste any public GitHub repo at fix-my-slop.vercel.app.

Frontier models are great at fixing slop and bad at noticing their own. They write the purple gradient because it's the statistical default; they elide code when an edit gets long; they import packages that sound right. FixMySlop is the other half of the loop:

repositories.description: INFRA-COMPASS is a tool that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to create and maintain an inventory of state and local codes and ordinances applicable to energy infrastructure.

paragraphs: COMPASS (formally the Infrastructure Continuous Ordinance Mapping for Planning and Siting Systems, or "INFRA-COMPASS") is an innovative software tool that harnesses the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the compilation and continued maintenance of an inventory of state and local codes and ordinances pertaining to energy infrastructure.

At a high level, COMPASS does two things: it retrieves the right ordinance documents for each jurisdiction you ask about, and then extracts structured data from those documents into a versioned database that downstream users can query as a CSV, Excel workbook, or GeoPackage.
What makes COMPASS different from simply asking ChatGPT for ordinance data is the architecture around the LLM call:
features: Structured, downstream-ready output — consistent CSV rows with stable column
Hallucination guardrails — cleaned text is checked against the source and dropped
Source-URL traceability — every record carries a URL back to the original
Cost control — cheap heuristic filters reject obviously irrelevant text before

paragraphs: Mathly is live but still early and the Arabic side is still far from complete!

I always liked math but it was hard for others to understand it, and for me sometimes. The problem with traditional math is it's just reading or listening to a teacher explain it on a whiteboard, which might not click with everyone. Thanks to people like 3Blue1Brown who inspired some of this.

So I built a platform where it's all based on interactivity. I've been using it myself to teach myself some of the math I get in school. You drag a point along a curve and watch the tangent follow. You build an equation one piece at a time. You sketch a graph before the answer is revealed. When you get something wrong, the lesson doesn't just say "try again", it takes a detour to walk you through exactly what you missed, then puts you back where you were.

repositories.name: wordcraft-react
repositories.description: Adaptation of Storytold's 1:1 reproduction of Microsoft Word. Original repo: https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft.

paragraphs: The WordCraft word processor, an open-source look-alike of Microsoft Word, packaged as an editor you can drop into React, Next.js or any web app, the way you would use TipTap or another WYSIWYG editor.

It isn't a re-implementation. The package ships the upstream WordCraft code itself (the ribbon, the dialogs, the page layout and the document engine), compiled from Rust to WebAssembly and pinned to one upstream commit. So what your users see is a 1:1 match with WordCraft's own web and desktop apps. What this package adds is the part an embedder needs: it mounts the editor in an element you own, gives you an API for documents and commands, and lets you handle saving instead of having the browser download a file.

whatItDoes.text: The WordCraft word processor, an open-source look-alike of Microsoft Word, packaged as an editor you can drop into React, Next.js or any web app, the way you would use TipTap or another WYSIWYG editor.

paragraphs: Talk for sixty seconds at the end of your work. Get every update you owe, each sentence checked against the code.

Every developer ends the day writing commits, a PR description, ticket comments, a standup and reports about work already done, and the why is the first thing to go. repositories.name: fractal-darkroom

paragraphs: Long-exposure photographs of mathematical escape — developed in a darkroom made of counting. A Buddhabrot family renderer: instead of asking "does this point escape?", it asks "where does it travel on the way out?" — and plots millions of escaping orbits as a density image. Plus 17 sibling fractals grown from the same idea: Antibuddhabrot, Nebulabrot, power mandalas (z³/z⁴/z⁵), Burning Ship, Tricorn, Celtic, Buffalo, sin/cos entire-function brots, Julia-brot, and a family of custom cosine/tan/sinh/exp mutations.
Every image on this page is a 2-D histogram of orbit visitation counts — no raytracing, no painting, just z ↦ z² + c iterated a few hundred million times.

In-browser encoding is CPU- and memory-bound: wasm FFmpeg is single-threaded here and the whole filesystem lives in RAM (with a 2 GB address-space ceiling). 1280×720@30 renders reliably at roughly real-time speed on ordinary hardware; 1080p roughly doubles pixel throughput and memory pressure, turning "works everywhere" into "works on fast machines with patience."

RenderSettings already models width/height/fps, so adding a 1920×1080 option later is a settings-UI change plus a memory warning — no pipeline changes. Cloud rendering (see roadmap) is the honest path to fast high-res exports.

repositories.description: Free OTP QR code generator and verifier for 2FA: make TOTP/HOTP otpauth:// QR codes for Google Authenticator, Authy, FreeOTP and more, then verify the codes. Runs in your browser.

paragraphs: A free, open-source OTP QR code generator and verifier for two-factor authentication (2FA). Make TOTP and HOTP otpauth:// QR codes for Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy, FreeOTP, 1Password, Bitwarden and other authenticator apps, then check that the app produces the right codes. Everything runs in your browser.

Setting up two-factor authentication by hand, for a test account, a shared service login or a server you run, means writing an otpauth:// URI and turning it into a QR code. The usual tool for that is the FreeOTP QR generator. It makes the QR code but stops there:

OTP QR Studio adds a verify step that runs the same RFC 4226/6238 maths as the server would, a random account name, a styled QR code with PNG and SVG downloads, and a page that doesn't make network requests.
features: No verification. You scan the code and hope. If the algorithm, digit count or period isn't one your app supports, or your phone's clock is off, you only find out when a real login fails.
Your name goes in the QR. The account field is free text, so it usually ends up holding your email.
Dated UI and a plain black-and-white QR code that you can't download.

repositories.name: treasury-proof-of-reserves
repositories.description: Regtest demo of a bitcoin-treasury proof of reserves: BIP-322 asset proofs and a Merkle-sum liability tree.

paragraphs: A company that holds bitcoin can publish one file that lets anyone check that its coins cover the debts it lists. This repo builds and checks that file for a made-up company on a private test network.

This repository builds and verifies a proof-of-reserves bundle for a fictional bitcoin-treasury company on a local Bitcoin Core regtest node. The asset side is BIP-322 signatures over a challenge that contains a block hash, checked against balances recomputed from the chain at that height. The liability side is a Merkle-sum tree over debt and preferred-stock instruments, with an inclusion proof per instrument. The output is one JSON bundle that a CLI or a static web page verifies, plus a written threat model of what the proof does and does not show.

whatItDoes.text: A company that holds bitcoin can publish one file that lets anyone check that its coins cover the debts it lists. This repo builds and checks that file for a made-up company on a private test network.

Underneath it's real double-entry accounting, so your budget, balances and net worth are all derived from one journal and can never drift out of balance. Your data lives in a single file you own — no cloud, no account, no tracking — and can be protected with strong password encryption, so even the file on disk is unreadable without your passphrase.
features: 🎯 Zero-based budgeting — the heart of the app. Every month, give each category a job until Ready to Assign reaches zero. Track Assigned · Activity · Available per category, with envelope balances that roll forward and…

💰 A Ready-to-Assign that's honest — it's a single pool drawn from your real on-budget account balances (assets net of credit-card debt), so money assigned to any month — even a future one — draws it down, and you can…

💳 Credit cards done right — spending on a card depletes its envelope and nets against the budget, so it's budget-neutral the way a good ZBB tool should be. Mark investments or a mortgage as off-budget so they count…
🔒 Locked history — past months are view-only; you budget the current month and beyond, and a budget you've already lived through can't be rewritten.

📒 Real double-entry accounting under the hood — every transaction is balanced postings that sum to zero, so your budget, balances and net worth are derived from one journal and can never go inconsistent.

repositories.name: Heisenbug
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: Heisenbug is a technical assessment platform where candidates fix real-world, ticket-style engineering bugs—such as concurrency races, machine learning data leakage, cross-site scripting (XSS), and database N+1 query bottlenecks—instead of solving algorithmic trivia. In verified environments (local development and GitHub Actions CI), candidate code is executed and graded inside isolated Docker containers that candidates never see. In environments lacking Docker daemon access (such as the live Render demo), the platform explicitly detects the missing daemon, executes visible tests in…
Currently, 5 of 5 production problem packs are fully seeded and published in the database across three engineering tracks:
features: Backend: Checkout double-charges on client retry (be-idempotency-001) — Node/Express, idempotency keys, distributed concurrency.
Backend: Inventory oversells during a flash sale (be-race-002) — Transaction isolation, race conditions, atomic conditional updates.
Backend: Optimize N+1 Query in Order History API (be-nplusone-001) — Relational batch fetching, query optimization (restored and published in the production database).
Security: Comment previews execute attacker-controlled HTML (sec-xss-001) — Stored/DOM XSS, input sanitization, safe DOM sinks.
Machine Learning: Churn model scores 96% in testing, barely beats a coin flip in production (ml-leakage-001) — Data leakage, temporal train/test splitting, baseline calibration.

Meet Blip: a mouse pointer that came alive and does things on your computer for you. It's the app's mascot, and it shows what each bot is doing. paragraphs: A soft, personal digital journal for your pregnancy journey — milestones, photos and memories, gently captured week by week as your little one blossoms.

Turn 40-ish weeks of quiet waiting into a keepsake you'll treasure forever. No timers, no clinical charts — just a warm, handcrafted place to hold every first kick, every scan, every "hurry up, little one" and all the love in between.

I searched. A lot. Up and down, across dozens of apps and journal platforms — and I kept coming up empty. So much of what's out there for this season of life is cold and clinical: charts, timers, "tracker" language, a nagging sense that you are the one being measured. I never found a journal that was genuinely lovely — warm in the way a hand-written letter is — that actually blossoms as the little one does, and that feels truly close to a mother's heart.
features: Everything is made to be completely customisable — your names, your little one's nickname, the due date, even the words on the cover. It's your story, told your way.
Add anything, any time. A page, a memory, a milestone — whenever the mood strikes, capture it the moment you love it.
Drag, drop, rearrange. Put the pages in exactly the order your heart wants them — it's your journal to shape.
The little things make it special — so we packed in a full set of thoughtful options that appear exactly when you want them.

repositories.description: [Technical Report] An End-to-End Multimodal GUI Agent for Real Mobile Environments

paragraphs: Trained and evaluated in a real-device closed loop — closing the benchmark-to-reality gap.

High benchmark scores do not reliably predict performance on real devices, where account states, permission dialogs, payment authentication, and risk-control mechanisms continually reshape the state distribution a GUI agent encounters. To close this gap, Xiaomi-GUI-0 is a native end-to-end multimodal GUI agent for real mobile environments, trained and evaluated within a real-device closed loop:
features: 📱 Real-device-dominant infrastructure: hundreds of physical phones, tablets, and in-vehicle cockpits, complemented by sandboxes, so collection, training, and evaluation share one real-deployment distribution.
🔁 Error-driven data flywheel: failure trajectories from real rollouts are converted into corrected actions, reflective rationales, and recovery demonstrations.
🎯 Progressive three-stage training: SFT → Step RL → Agentic RL incrementally builds basic interface operation, long-horizon planning, and error recovery.
🧪 RealMobile benchmark: 100 real-device tasks across 14 live apps, scored by fine-grained sub-goals, with 57% spanning multiple applications.

whatItDoes.text: Trained and evaluated in a real-device closed loop — closing the benchmark-to-reality gap.

repositories.name: Xiaomi-Lens-0
repositories.description: [Technical Report] Locate, Segment, and Reason.

paragraphs: Pixel-level grounding and visual reasoning in a compact 4B multimodal model.
News · What it does · Method · Showcases · Results · Quick Start · Citation

Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal large language model that learns from pixel-level supervision through a shared visual backbone. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B, it decodes each generated token into a mask with a lightweight decoder, so the same model that answers in text can point at the regions it refers to, in a final answer or in the middle of its reasoning. It improves referring comprehension over Qwen3.5-4B by 5.6 points on average across eight RefCOCO-family splits and improves scores on all eight fine-grained perception benchmarks.

paragraphs: A Gemini agent that checks whether a grocery product has shrunk and works out how much more you now pay per unit.
I built it for the Google Cloud Rapid Agent Hackathon (Elastic track) in three days, with Google ADK, Gemini, Elasticsearch and the Elastic MCP server.

Shrinkflation is when a product gets smaller and the price stays the same. It's an economic idea that has interested me for a long time. A lot of companies use it to make any tiny bit of extra profit they can, and a smaller bag at the same price is easy to miss. Capital One Shopping research estimates it has touched roughly a third of grocery items. The number that shows it is the price per ounce, so that's what this agent reports.

repositories.name: tinyworldformer
repositories.description: Tiny world model generates games and stream ac plays them all on Pico 2W

paragraphs: Using 2 small neural networks to generate and play the game at the same time on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. The first one creates the game: given the current frame and the action, it predicts the next frame and the reward. The second one plays that game: it uses the generated frame and picks an action.
Every frame above was sampled by the world model network, and the actions were taken by the actor network.

I got interested in looped transformers, where one transformer block is applied several times with the same weights instead of stacking different layers. Reusing weights is cheap on memory, so I wanted to see if a looped world model could be small enough to run on a microcontroller. I picked the Pico 2 W because it is cheap and has an FPU, and small games because I could write the real versions directly into numpy and check every generated frame against them. Later I added a streaming RL agent so the board could also learn to play inside its own dream.

paragraphs: A desktop workstation for reverse-engineering a CAN bus.

Load a capture, work out which bytes carry what, write the signal definitions down, check them against real frames, and export a DBC that other tools can read. It also speaks the diagnostic protocols (UDS, ISO-TP, J1939, OBD-II, XCP, DoIP), and, for isolated bench use only, can inject, replay, fuzz and bridge.

Status: beta. Single-author project, actively developed. It runs, and the behaviour described here is covered by an automated suite of 578 tests (see Testing). But the analysis methods are heuristics that suggest candidates rather than identify signals, some features need optional dependencies, and it has not been validated across a wide range of real vehicles. Read Limitations before relying on a result.

repositories.name: Ruumble
repositories.description: Your Mumble server as an office building: web UI with presence, one-click room changes and a comprehensive board in every room

paragraphs: Your Mumble server as an office building. Ruumble is a web UI next to the regular Mumble client: the channels become floors and rooms, you see at a glance who sits where and who is talking, you move to another room with a click, and every room has a board for notes, code, images and files. Voice stays in Mumble, and Mumble itself stays unchanged.

Ruumble is an add-on, not a standalone app. It needs a Mumble server that you run or administer, and it has two parts: - a small service (one Docker container) that the server operator runs next to the Mumble server. It needs access to the server's Ice interface and serves the web UI. - a plugin that every user installs once in their Mumble desktop client (Linux or Windows). Without your own Mumble server and the plugin in the clients there is nothing to see, except the demo below.
Try the demo: runs in the browser against a simulated server, no Mumble needed.
features: Building view: top-level channels become floors, second-level channels rooms, the floor channel itself the corridor. The order follows the channels' position in Mumble.
Presence: talking indicator, mute and deafen, quiet and away, listeners, recording, Mumble avatars.
One click to move: Ruumble moves your own Mumble client, and mute and deafen work from the browser too.

Board in every room: Markdown, source code with highlighting, images, files (10 MB by default), quick reactions, shared task lists, one post kept on top, search. The others in the room get a short notice in their Mumble…

Care for admins: whoever has Mumble's Write permission tends the stored data from a plant (delete old posts, export or move a board, tidy up after deleted rooms), changes the building's settings and revokes paired…

paragraphs: Rittenhouse Political stopped by Code for Philly in September 2015 to ask for help with a data set in CSV. Their goal is to outline the difference between male and female political representation in Pennsylvania based on election results between 2000-2014. They would like to visually display the data in tables, graphs, and ultimately a "heat map" to show how women have been represented in PA during those years. We are working in JavaScript to display this data in a palatable manner for end users.
There are two separate maps to display for the heat map. One shows the House of Representatives district lines, while the other shows the Senate District lines. See the links for the map outlines:

paragraphs: 量子計算模擬與跨語言對照：同一 .qc 電路驅動 C++17 / Python / JavaScript 三引擎，振幅機率一致到 1e-12（瀏覽器端即時重算並顯示偏差）。
同一份電路描述檔（.qc）驅動三個彼此獨立的態向量模擬器：C++17 核心、純 Python 套件、 以及可直接在瀏覽器裡執行的 JavaScript 引擎。三者的振幅與機率必須一致到 1e-12 以內， 一致性由 scripts/checkparity.py 實際比對產生，不是靠人工核對。
線上示範： 頁面載入預先產生的參考結果 docs/reference.json，在瀏覽器內用 JavaScript 引擎重算同一批 電路，並當場顯示兩邊的偏差；離線後仍可透過 Service Worker 開啟。

repositories.description: Verify evidence integrity offline with SHA-256 manifests and Ed25519 signatures.

paragraphs: Detect any change to a folder of evidence files, and check who signed it, without a server.

e3bundle records the SHA-256 of every file in a directory, lets one or more people sign that manifest with Ed25519, and verifies the result offline: changed, missing or added files and forged or stale signatures are reported in a machine-readable JSON report with a clear exit code.
It is part of the E3-001 public protocol of CASTÚO-SYSTEM, but it works on any directory and needs nothing from CASTÚO.

paragraphs: End-to-end MLOps pipeline that predicts Polish apartment prices from the public Kaggle dataset — versioned data, validated contracts, training with conformal intervals and experiment tracking, a registry-backed inference API, a Streamlit demo, and drift monitoring. repositories.name: Apparelflow-Gatekeeper
repositories.description: Full-stack ERP module for apparel manufacturing that manages cutting orders, component verification, role-based access control (RBAC), audit logging, and secure batch release to the sewing queue.

paragraphs: A production batch verification gate for a garment factory. Cutting orders move from the cutting floor to the sewing line only after a verifier counts every component against the recipe's bill of materials — with a strict, database-enforced state machine and an immutable audit trail.

Built as a modular monolith: one Next.js deploy, thin API route handlers, pure shared business rules in domain/, and a Supabase Postgres database that enforces the lifecycle at the schema level (triggers, checks, row-level security).
The system was deliberately built as a modular monolith. The alternatives were rejected for concrete reasons:
features: Role-based sign-in & one-click demo accounts — httpOnly cookie session, 8-hour JWT, live role switcher in the header.
Order creation from recipes — the server computes expected piece counts and expected fabric from the recipe multiplier and snapshots them per order.

Supervisor dashboard cards — a summary strip of four filter cards: Total / Pending / Verified / Rejected. Each card shows a live count and acts as a filter — click it to narrow the order table. Click the active card…

Verifier terminal — per-order counting with a live traffic-light (GREEN / YELLOW / RED / UNCOUNTED) updated from the same rules the server uses, plus a server hard stop that returns 422 on any shortage or uncounted row.

Verifier history tables — the verifier page lists Verified orders (order, verifier, wastage %) and Rejected orders (attempt number and the rejection reason) pulled from the immutable verificationlogs audit trail — see…

whatItDoes.text: A production batch verification gate for a garment factory. Cutting orders move from the cutting floor to the sewing line only after a verifier counts every component against the recipe's bill of materials — with a strict, database-enforced state machine and an immutable audit trail.

requirements.text: Role-based sign-in & one-click demo accounts — httpOnly cookie session, 8-hour JWT, live role switcher in the header.
Login hardening — one generic Invalid email or password message, a dummy bcrypt compare against unknown emails (no timing oracle), and a 5-failure / 15-minute per-account lockout persisted in the DB.

repositories.description: A Python Library for orthographic normalization and diacritic restoration for Yorùbá text. Separates tone marks from underdots. It has zero dependencies with a CLI and a web demo.

paragraphs: Orthographic normalization and diacritic handling for Yorùbá text. Zero runtime dependencies. Requires Python 3.9 or newer.

I had just finished the experiments for a paper comparing zero-shot prompting against fine-tuned models on Yorùbá sentiment analysis. Part of that work involved stripping diacritics from the text. Writing that preprocessing, I kept hitting the same problem in every tool I looked at. They treated tone marks and the underdot in ẹ, ọ, ṣ as one category called "diacritics" and removed both together.
They are not the same thing. The underdot changes the word. ẹ and e are different letters. Tone marks sit on top of a vowel and do not change which word it is.

paragraphs: A tech blog wired for Supabase and AdSense: index.html (list), post.html (live/preview article view), and pre-rendered pages under posts/ that are what actually get indexed and shared.

post.html?slug=... renders everything client-side after fetching from Supabase — great for instant previews, bad for SEO and AdSense review, because the raw HTML any crawler (or non-JS tool) sees is just a "Loading article…" shell with a generic, identical title/description on every article. That reads as duplicate/thin content and is one of the most common reasons AdSense applications get rejected.

scripts/build-posts.mjs fixes this by generating one real, pre-rendered HTML file per published post (posts/.html) with the actual headline, byline, body text, canonical URL, Open Graph tags, and Article structured data baked in — no JavaScript required to read it. post.html?slug=... still works (handy for previewing a post right after writing it, before the next rebuild), but its canonical tag and all share links now point at the pre-rendered posts/.html version, so Google only ever indexes one, real, unique page per article.

whatItDoes.text: A tech blog wired for Supabase and AdSense: index.html (list), post.html (live/preview article view), and pre-rendered pages under posts/ that are what actually get indexed and shared.

paragraphs: A minimal Vercel Edge Function that relays XHTTP traffic to your backend Xray/V2Ray server. Use Vercel's globally distributed edge network (and its vercel.com / .vercel.app SNI) as a front for your real Xray endpoint — useful in regions where the backend host is blocked but Vercel is reachable.

⚠️ XHTTP transport only. This relay is purpose-built for Xray's xhttp transport. It will not work with WebSocket, gRPC, TCP, mKCP, QUIC, or any other V2Ray/Xray transport — the Edge runtime doesn't support WebSocket upgrade or arbitrary TCP, and the other transports rely on protocol features Edge fetch doesn't expose.
fetch(..., { duplex: "half" }) → upstream response). First byte out as soon as first byte in. This matches XHTTP's chunked POST/GET model exactly.

repositories.name: cachet-showcase
repositories.description: Showcase and interactive demo for Cachet, centrally managed email signatures for Microsoft 365 and Outlook. Designed and developed by Alyssa I. Agard. Source code is hosted in a private repository.

paragraphs: Try the interactive demo · Read how I built it

An email signature is part of an organization's public record. It carries the organization's name and brand, each person's role and contact details, and often a legal disclaimer. Without central management, every signature depends on each person configuring it correctly on every device and keeping it current. Shared mailboxes and phones make that harder.

Commercial signature services charge per user, every month, which is hard to justify for a small nonprofit. I wanted a solution that Agard Research Associates Inc. could run at a fraction of that cost and that could later become a product for other organizations.
features: Efficiency. One change reaches everyone. New staff get the right signature as soon as they appear in the directory, with no setup and no help desk request.

Compliance. Required information and disclaimers appear on every message, including those sent from phones and shared mailboxes, with a server-side safety net ready for anything the add-in cannot reach.
Uniformity. Everyone presents the organization the same way, in email-safe markup that displays consistently across mail programs.

index.html is the interactive demo, published with GitHub Pages. It is a standalone simulation with a fictional organization and sample people, so anyone can try Cachet without signing in to Microsoft 365.
METHODOLOGY.md explains how Cachet was planned, designed, secured, tested, and deployed.

repositories.description: What time is it in Babylon? A live, Antikythera-inspired clock for 13 calendars of the ancient world, oracle-tested.

paragraphs: What time is it in Babylon? A live, Antikythera-inspired clock for the calendars of the ancient world — and a small, tested TypeScript library behind it.

A date can change its meaning when its calendar is left unstated. The Ides of March, 44 BCE are a Julian date, not a proleptic Gregorian one. In a Chinese leap year, a month number can occur twice: 2033 has both a regular and a leap month 11.

Horologium moves one instant through these different reckonings. Each calendar names its method and marks projections outside its historical era. The Chinese lunar-year inspector shows the month boundaries and solar terms behind a leap-month decision. The arithmetic and astronomical limits are documented alongside the results.
features: 13 calendar systems with real epochs, real leap-year/intercalation

rules, and native-script rendering where it applies: Julian Day and the proleptic Gregorian/Julian calendars, Roman (Kalends/Nones/Ides, AUC, Roman numerals, seasonal hours), Byzantine Anno Mundi + Indiction, Islamic…
Astronomy: Sun/Moon position and phase, the tropical zodiac, the five
naked-eye planets (Standish/JPL Keplerian elements), and the Metonic/ Callippic/Saros/Exeligmos cycles behind the Antikythera mechanism's back dials.
A bronze, animated dial — zodiac ring, Egyptian 365-day ring, Sun/Moon

whatItDoes.text: What time is it in Babylon? A live, Antikythera-inspired clock for the calendars of the ancient world — and a small, tested TypeScript library behind it.

repositories.name: Eco_Loop
repositories.description: Autonomous closed-loop HVAC control: a live EnergyPlus simulation supervised by a local open-source LLM over the Model Context Protocol. Setpoints are injected into the running solver - no IDF rewrite, no restart. 8.5% HVAC energy saved while holding thermal comfort. Demo: https://www.loom.com/share/cd6b6eea292747a3bbe7087e8b16ab78

paragraphs: A building that runs itself. EnergyPlus supplies the physics, a local open-source LLM supplies the judgement, and the Model Context Protocol carries every reading and every command between them — while the simulation is still running.
▶ Watch the demo · Live dashboard · Architecture

Traditional building management systems follow rigid clock schedules. Eco-Loop turns the building into a self-correcting agent: sensors are read every zone timestep, the aggregated state goes to the LLM through six MCP tools once per control interval, and the validated setpoints are written straight into the live solver through the EnergyPlus actuator API — no IDF rewrite, no restart, so the loop closes inside a single simulation.

whatItDoes.text: A building that runs itself. EnergyPlus supplies the physics, a local open-source LLM supplies the judgement, and the Model Context Protocol carries every reading and every command between them — while the simulation is still running.

repositories.name: sba-loan-default-prediction
repositories.description: XGBoost default risk on 890K SBA loans, AUCPR 0.567, cost-weighted threshold and calibration disclosed, live scoring app.

paragraphs: The same Gradio app the Hugging Face Space serves, here from the Docker image at /ui. The threshold radio exposes the cost-optimal 0.35 next to the model-card 0.66, and the calibration warning is on the page, not in a footnote.

A production XGBoost classifier that scores U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) 7(a) loan applications for default risk, shipped as a live Gradio app on Hugging Face Spaces. Built around an explicit, audited eval pipeline (learning curves, residual analysis, confusion matrices, ensemble weight search) and an interpretability layer (SHAP bar/beeswarm/waterfall, permutation importance, surrogate decision tree) designed for stakeholder review, not just a leaderboard score. Version 1.1 adds what a reviewer asks for next: a held-out evaluation that reproduces the headline and then measures…

This project started as a graduate Machine Learning coursework assignment at UT Dallas in early 2026. The dataset, the broad modeling constraint (two-XGBoost ensemble, AUCPR optimization, scoring-contract requirements), and the deployment requirement came from that assignment brief, preserved as problembrief.md. Everything else, the feature engineering decisions, the ensemble weight search and the honest-disclosure framing of the result, the SHAP and surrogate-tree interpretability layer, the operational framing around AUCPR, the production scoring contract, the failure-mode analysis, and the…
features: 16 raw: State, Zip, BankState, NAICS, NoEmp, NewExist, CreateJob, RetainedJob, FranchiseCode, UrbanRural, RevLineCr, LowDoc, DisbursementGross, BalanceGross, GrAppv, SBAAppv.
15 derived (stateless, same logic in notebook and scoring module):
Ratios: sbacoverageratio (SBA guarantee / requested), disbursementratio (disbursed / approved), balanceratio, sbatodisbursementratio, jobsperemployee.

Log transforms: logdisbursement, logemployees (taming heavy right tails before tree splitting on monotonic transforms, XGBoost is invariant to monotonic transforms in theory but the log forms also stabilize quantile…
Flags: isfranchise, newbusiness, samestatebank, revlineflag, lowdocflag, naicsunknown.

repositories.name: three-dlss-nr
repositories.description: A Three.js (TSL / WebGPU) port of OpenDLSS-NR, the open-source reimplementation of NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural rendering network

paragraphs: A port to Three.js (TSL / WebGPU) of OpenDLSS-NR by maan. OpenDLSS-NR is an open-source reimplementation of the network behind NVIDIA's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering. All credit for that reimplementation, its numerics and its documentation belongs to OpenDLSS-NR. This repository ports it to three.js and tracks upstream commit 9d08f41, included as the reference/OpenDLSS-NR submodule. Not affiliated with NVIDIA, and no NVIDIA weights are included (details).

The DLSS 5 neural rendering network, as three.js compute nodes, byte for byte. three-dlss-nr runs the 71-block OpenDLSS-NR network as TSL compute kernels inside a WebGPURenderer, fed straight from your three.js scene with no CPU readback. Every intermediate tensor is byte-identical to the reference WebGPU port.

Synthetic weights: output is not meaningful. The demo in split view on the TSL backend, NR off on the left and NR on on the right. Synthetic weights have the right layout and run the network's real arithmetic, but the image they produce means nothing, hence the red field (why). With a real model directory the right half is the re-rendered head. Head: Lee Perry-Smith, CC BY 3.0 (credits).
features: They prove the port computes the same function as the reference. The port is bit-exact against the reference
They let the whole pipeline run end to end in the tests and in the demo.

repositories.name: awesome-bitcoin-blake
repositories.description: A curated list of nodes, wallets, servers, explorers, pools and docs for the Bitcoin BLAKE2b chain

paragraphs: A curated list of nodes, wallets, servers, explorers, pools, tools and docs for the Bitcoin BLAKE2b chain.

On 8 August 2026 Bitcoin Knots nodes enforcing BIP-110 (the Reduced Data Temporary Softfork, RDTS) parted from the SHA256d chain at block 961,632. That branch produced only eight blocks in three weeks. On 30 August 2026, at block 961,640, it changed proof-of-work from SHA256d to BLAKE2b (Knots PR #359). Block headers are now 164 bytes (header v2), so most existing wallets, Electrum servers and explorers need patches to follow the chain. This list tracks what works today.

Everything here is community maintained. Verify releases and signatures yourself. Listing is not an endorsement. Flags in italics mark experimental, testnet-only, closed-source or unmaintained entries.

whatItDoes.text: A curated list of nodes, wallets, servers, explorers, pools, tools and docs for the Bitcoin BLAKE2b chain.

Live demo · Quick start · Install options · Security · Website

repositories.name: ceems
repositories.description: A Prometheus exporter and a REST API server to export metrics of compute units of resource managers like SLURM, LSF, Openstack, k8s

paragraphs: Compute Energy & Emissions Monitoring Stack (CEEMS) (pronounced as kiːms) contains a Prometheus exporter to export metrics of compute instance units and a REST API server that serves the metadata and aggregated metrics of each compute unit. Optionally, it includes a TSDB load balancer that supports basic access control on TSDB so that one user cannot access metrics of another user.

"Compute Unit" in the current context has a wider scope. It can be a batch job in HPC, a VM in cloud, a pod in k8s, etc. The main objective of the repository is to quantify the energy consumed and estimate emissions by each "compute unit". The repository itself does not provide any frontend apps to show dashboards and it is meant to use along with Grafana and Prometheus to show statistics to users.

Although CEEMS was born out of a need to monitor energy and carbon footprint of compute workloads, it supports monitoring performance metrics as well. In addition, it leverages eBPF framework to monitor IO and network metrics in a resource manager agnostic way. It also supports eBPF based zero instrumentation continuous profiling of compute units.
features: Monitors energy, performance, IO and network metrics for different types of resource
managers (SLURM, LSF, Openstack, k8s)
Supports different energy sources like RAPL, HWMON, Cray's PM Counters and BMC via IPMI or Redfish
Supports NVIDIA (MIG, time sharing, MPS and vGPU) and AMD GPUs (Partition like CPX, QPX, TPX, DPX)
and also supports Dynamic MIG offered by k8s DRA for NVIDIA GPUs.

whatItDoes.text: Compute Energy & Emissions Monitoring Stack (CEEMS) (pronounced as kiːms) contains a Prometheus exporter to export metrics of compute instance units and a REST API server that serves the metadata and aggregated metrics of each compute unit. repositories.name: celox
repositories.description: Celox HDL Simulator

paragraphs: A compiler-based RTL simulator for Veryl and a synthesizable subset of SystemVerilog.

Celox compiles an elaborated Veryl design into executable simulation kernels and exposes the design through a type-safe TypeScript API. The same kernels can be built from synthesizable SystemVerilog through the Rust API (see SystemVerilog support). It is both a practical way to test RTL with Vitest and an open testbed for exploring how RTL simulators should be structured.

Celox explores a simple question: what does a modern RTL simulator architecture look like when compilation, scheduling, state representation, code generation, and testbench integration are designed together?
features: Veryl-specific analysis ends at a source-independent design representation.
Combinational dependencies and clock domains are scheduled before execution.
A backend-independent IR and state layout are shared by multiple code
Native and WebAssembly execution use the same runtime contract.
The testbench sees the same typed design API regardless of the execution

repositories.description: Injects realistic failures into AI agents — broken connectors, expired auth, prompt injection, schema drift, truncated payloads — and judges from tool-boundary evidence whether the agent reported the truth.

paragraphs: Chaos engineering for AI agents. Injects connector failures, expired auth, prompt injection, tool schema drift and truncated payloads, then judges from tool-boundary evidence whether the agent told the user the truth — not from what it claims. Ships a CI gate, a GitHub Action, an MCP server and a headless suite runner.
Live demo · Getting started · Evaluate in 3 minutes · Quick start · Leaderboard · Direct Line · GitHub Action · Deploy to Azure · Resilience laboratory

AI agents can fabricate success after tool failures, allowing silently broken workflows to ship. There is no standard way to test whether an agent recognizes those failures and recovers safely. This is not a model-quality problem you can prompt away: 2 of 4 benchmarked agents reported success to the user after the connector returned HTTP 401 (measured, not asserted).

repositories.name: OxyBook
repositories.description: Self-hosted docs platform: edit the markdown/MDX in your GitHub repo from the browser, propose changes as pull requests, publish a static site on merge. Early alpha.

paragraphs: A self-hostable documentation platform where the git repository is the source of truth. Writers edit pages in the browser; every change becomes a pull request in your GitHub repository; merged changes publish a static documentation site.

Status: early alpha, looking for testers. There is no release yet, and things will break. What works today, end to end on a real GitHub repository: - Connect a repository through a GitHub App that OxyBook creates for you. - Sync its markdown and MDX into OxyBook, and publish a static site with navigation, search, and redirects for renamed pages. - Edit pages in the browser (source mode, with live preview and autosave), review the exact diff, and propose it: OxyBook opens a pull request on an oxybook/ branch. If you link your GitHub account, the pull request is yours; otherwise the App opens…

Also relevant: AFFiNE is MIT-licensed except its backend packages, which need a paid EE subscription to run in production. Material for MkDocs is in maintenance mode with end of life announced for 5 May 2027; its users need somewhere to go, and OxyBook preserves their MkDocs-specific syntax as raw blocks from v1 on.
features: GitHub App integration: webhook-driven sync with periodic reconciliation; changes go out as pull requests in your repository.
Block editor (TipTap/ProseMirror): headings, lists, task lists, tables, code blocks, images, links, callouts (:::note directives and GitHub > [!NOTE] alerts).

Lossless round-trip: unedited blocks keep their exact bytes; MDX/JSX, raw HTML, unknown directives and unparseable frontmatter are preserved as read-only raw blocks; source mode for anything else. Enforced by an…
Drafts with autosave, exact diff preview before proposing, follow-up commits to an open PR, optional DCO Signed-off-by trailer.
Automatic three-way merge when the base branch moves, plus a block-level conflict view.

whatItDoes.text: A self-hostable documentation platform where the git repository is the source of truth. Writers edit pages in the browser; every change becomes a pull request in your GitHub repository; merged changes publish a static documentation site.

requirements.text: You need Docker with Compose v2, a GitHub account, and a test repository with a few markdown files in a folder such as docs/.

paragraphs: Display test patterns and calibration aids for OLED, IPS, and mobile screens, running entirely in your browser.

Test videos are compressed. Codecs smear near-black detail and add banding and blocking, which are exactly the artifacts you're trying to spot. PanelProbe draws every pattern losslessly to a canvas mapped 1:1 to your device pixels. There's nothing to install and nothing leaves your machine.
features: 26 test patterns in five categories, each with a one-key shortcut.
Test All steps through the 24 non-strobe tests automatically — 10 seconds each, with pause and skip.
Guided Wizard walks you through nine pass/issue checks. It produces a report you can print or save as PDF, or export as JSON, with advice for each issue.
True 1:1 pixel mapping. The canvas backing store follows the device-pixel content box, so it stays exact even at fractional scaling (125%, 150%).
Refresh-rate detection snaps to common panel rates (60–540 Hz). Motion tests render at the native rate.
